lessons.subtitle: CLOSED SYLLABLES & VC/CV RULE
lessons.introText: A closed syllable ends with a consonant. Its vowel is short because it is trapped between consonants. To divide a word with two consonants between vowels, split between the consonants (VC/CV rule). This is the Rabbit Rule. Listen for the short vowel sounds and practice splitting.

lessons.subtitle: OPEN SYLLABLES & V/CV RULE
lessons.introText: An open syllable ends with a vowel. Its vowel is long because it is free at the end. To divide a word with one consonant between vowels, split before the consonant (V/CV rule). This is the Tiger Rule. Listen for the long vowel sounds and practice splitting.
